recovered_mathematical_scope.baseline: Tao V7 Proposition 1.11; V5 comparison is audit history, not the main contribution.
recovered_mathematical_scope.common_base: Fix b>=s_* and alpha=1001/1000; t_j=b^(alpha^j); use the same inputs mu_(t_(j+1)) for every real x>=1.
recovered_mathematical_scope.first_entry_family: K_x mu_(t_(j+1)) converges on E_x=(positive odds<=x) union {dagger}. The unhalved l1 error is at most L_c(log t_j)^(-c), uniformly for 1<=x<=t_j, where L_c=B'/(1-alpha^(-c)).
recovered_mathematical_scope.compatibility: K_x lambda_y^infinity=lambda_x^infinity for every 1<=x<=y; thresholds need not belong to the scale sequence.
recovered_mathematical_scope.finite_joint_laws: For any finite ordered thresholds x_1<=...<=x_r, r>=1, J(z)=(p_x1(z),...,p_xr(z)) is a bijection from E_xr to compatible tuples, with last-coordinate inverse and singleton fibres. Its pushforward is an l1 isometry; joint convergence has the same bound as the largest-threshold law, with no factor in r.
recovered_mathematical_scope.phase_boundary: Changing b to b^(alpha^k) for k>=0 removes a finite prefix and preserves the family. Equality for arbitrary different bases is not established.
nonclaims: No stronger quantitative orbit-minimum theorem; that result remains Tao's Theorem 3.1.
No independent reproof or formalization of the full Fourier-renewal chain.
No finite certificate proves analytic convergence; saved finite checks test exact finite algebra.
No arbitrary-base independence, dynamical invariant law, Collatz convergence, or literature-priority claim.
